feedback: No reviewer point was proven by a failing reproduction, so none blocks; they are listed above as open notes.
unproven: Footer component (src/components/Footer.tsx) still includes the <nav aria-label="Footer" className="footer-nav"> which contains only the Services and Company columns – but there is no indication that the extra unlabeled column of all page links (Services, Systems, Training, Engagements, About, Contact) has been removed from the DOM. The current markup does not show any such column, but the task expects the footer to contain exactly three groups: the brand group (wordmark, text, email), a Services column with five specific links (AI Enablement, Training, Custom Development, Systems engineering, Engagements), and a Company column with About and Contact. The current SERVICE_LINKS array includes only the required five links but does not include the correct link labels (AI Enablement vs "AI Enablement" is correct) and order. However, the test likely expects the presence of a third column (the extra unlabeled column) to be absent. Since there is no fourth column present in the source, the issue may stem from CSS: the global.css does not define a 3‑track grid for the footer at desktop breakpoints, nor a stacked layout for phones. Without appropriate CSS, the footer groups may not be laid out as required (brand group wider on desktop, stacked on phones). The current CSS lacks any rules for .footer-inner or .footer-brand/.footer-nav grid layout, so the layout requirements R10 and R11 may not be satisfied. Add a CSS grid (e.g., .footer-inner { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 2fr 1fr 1fr; gap: 48px; } and modify with a media query for phones to stack) and ensure the three groups are correctly spaced and ordered. Also ensure the copyright line remains below a hairline after the grid.

Contact page (src/pages/ContactPage.tsx) does not contain the navy page header band with the data‑grid motif, eyebrow "CONTACT", h1 "Book a consultation", lead text, and mailto line as required by R12‑R20. The current ContactPage likely renders the form directly without that header band. Add a page‑header component (reuse the existing band used on other inner pages) with the required content and move the form section below it, preserving the existing IDs, labels and behavior.

Systems page hero layout (src/pages/SystemsPage.tsx) currently places the architecture diagram below the heading and lead sentence (as per the original design) and does not wrap the text and diagram in a grid that places them side‑by‑side on desktop. The task requires a two‑column grid with the text column (~40% width) left and the diagram (~60%) right, vertically centered, for screen widths >=1024px, and stacked for phones. Modify the SystemsPage to add the appropriate grid container and CSS (e.g., .systems-hero__grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0,2fr) minmax(0,3fr); align-items:center; } with a mobile fallback).
